title: Perimeter Access Regulator: Terraform security stack for SG / NACL / private DNS / egress proxy
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (perimeter-access-regulator) that standardizes VPC security controls across Private deployments: least-privilege Security Groups, default-deny NACL templates for subnets, private Route53 zone forwarding for internal resolution, and a pluggable egress policy layer that supports both managed NAT and an internal egress proxy (eProxy). The module must include module-level health-check outputs and Terraform-driven canary upgrade hooks to support safe rollouts in Dedicated/Private clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes configurable inputs for security groups, NACLs, private DNS zone IDs, egress-mode (nat | eproxy) and allowed egress CIDRs/domains
Default module deployment enforces deny-by-default NACL rules and minimal SG rules (control-plane only) for customer-managed subnets
Module publishes health_check outputs: 'sg_status', 'nacl_status', 'egress_proxy_health' suitable for automated checks (boolean/enum strings)
Automated CI runs terratest/inspec check verifying Terraform plan does not open unexpected ports and conftest policies pass
Module includes migration path and terraform state upgrade notes for v1 -> v2 with a documented canary strategy
Module documentation and examples added to internal Confluence and example repo (terraform-private-examples)
technical_notes: Security Groups modeled as resource 'aws_security_group' with nested module for common rules; use for_each to create per-service groups
NACLs created per-subnet with explicit stateless deny/allow rules; rely on positional rule numbers for stable ordering; document constraints to avoid overlapping rule collisions
Private DNS: use aws_route53_zone_association for VPC -> private zone and optional conditional forwarding via aws_route53_resolver_rule with target endpoint for on-prem DNS

Egress policy: support two modes: 'nat' (managed AWS NAT Gateway or customer-provided NAT) and 'eproxy' (customer-deployable proxy endpoint behind ALB/ASG). eProxy health checked via target-group health and custom /health API
Health outputs implemented as terraform null_resource triggers querying CloudWatch metric filters (or calling internal diagnostics endpoint) during apply when enabled
Keep module pure Terraform v1.9+ (HCL2), avoid provider alias complexity; where unavoidable, document provider alias patterns for multi-account deployments
Policy-as-code: include baseline Rego policies (conftest) to prevent public egress and ensure NACL deny defaults
Trade-offs considered: NAT is simpler but more permissive and costly; eProxy provides domain-level filtering and auditing but increases operational overhead
progress_updates: 2026-02-21: Initial design sync with Infra and Security teams. Agreed on two operational modes and health output contract (Priya, Omar, Elena).
2026-02-26: PoC Terraform module created in feature/perimeter-access-regulator branch; validates SG + NACL templates in sandbox account (Liam).

2026-03-03: Security review: requested explicit tenancy isolation flags and default logging to CloudWatch/central S3 for eProxy access logs. Action: add logging optional input (SEC team - review note).
2026-03-08: First terratest suite added (port scanning + DNS resolution checks). Found a race condition when associating private zone; added depends_on to resolve (Liam).
2026-03-12: Updated docs in Confluence and added example for in-place upgrade with canary subnets. Preparing PR for internal review.
review_feedback: SEC: Require KMS-encrypted S3 for eProxy logs and record key usage for audit
Platform: Add clear provider alias instructions for multi-account deployment; avoid cross-account resource creation in default path
PM: Add migration docs and a backwards-compatible toggle for old/narrow rule set to simplify customer upgrades
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfigured SG/NACL can block control-plane traffic. Mitigation: include a 'dry-run' terratest that verifies controller endpoints before applying to prod subnets
Risk: Rollout of eProxy could cause traffic failure. Mitigation: implement canary subnets and automatic rollback hooks in CI using health outputs
Risk: Cost of NAT Gateways. Mitigation: provide cost-estimate helper script and recommend eProxy for high-volume flows with domain filtering
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate + fmt + static conftest policy checks
Integration: terratest in sandbox to provision module and validate connectivity patterns (SSH blocked, HTTPS outbound allowed to whitelisted domains)
Chaos: simulated endpoint failure of eProxy target-group should trigger failover to NAT mode or block egress depending on customer policy
Security: run internal 3rd-party audit on final module before GA
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (Canary): deploy to 2 non-production clusters; enable health outputs and monitoring; run traffic soak for 72 hours
Stage 2 (Limited Prod): roll out to 10% of tenant subnets in Dedicated; monitor error budgets and latency impact for 7 days
Stage 3 (GA): flip default 'privnet_security_module' to enabled in new accounts and publish migration playbook for existing customers
qa_checks: Verify terraform plan shows only intended changes (no removal of existing control-plane SG rules)
Ensure private DNS zone association does not alter external resolution paths
Confirm health_check outputs return expected enum values after apply
Run conftest policies against generated plan to ensure no public egress CIDRs are introduced
